title: Eid al-Adha: sacrifice
hookLine: the sacrifice, the sharing, and what you'd give up for Allah
tomorrow: a king who could buy anything made his own armor. why?

cards: Ask someone what they'd give up for the person they love most, and the answers come fast: sleep, money, a weekend, a kidney. Ask what they'd give up for God, and people tend to go quiet.
Eid al-Adha, the festival of the sacrifice, is built on that question. In the Qur'an, Abraham sees in a dream that he is sacrificing his son. And he tells the son.

teach.h: DO THAT WHICH THOU ART COMMANDED.
teach.b: The son answers, in Pickthall's words: "O my father! Do that which thou art commanded." Both of them surrender.
Then God calls out that the vision is fulfilled: "Then We ransomed him with a tremendous victim." The passage doesn't name the son.

Muslim commentators such as Ibn Kathir say Ishmael; Genesis, read by Jews and Christians, tells the test with Isaac. One story, kept in more than one house, with a name that differs. So what was really given?
The Qur'an says it plainly about every Eid animal since: "Their flesh and their blood reach not Allah, but the devotion from you reacheth Him." And the meat doesn't sit in one freezer.
The Prophet ﷺ said of it: eat, feed others, and store some.
The sacrifice turns into a shared table, and the question stays with whoever's holding the knife, or the grocery bag.

how: On Eid al-Adha Muslims gather for the Eid prayer, and families who are able offer an animal in sacrifice, sharing the meat among the household, friends and people in need.

o: the day the pilgrims stand together on the plain
the festival that closes a whole month of fasting
the festival of sacrifice, remembering Abraham's test

games.q: the story and the feast — tap the pairs.
p: do that which thou art commanded
the devotion is what reaches God

s: the Qur'an's sacrifice passage names the son
it doesn't. commentators such as Ibn Kathir say Ishmael; Genesis names Isaac.
the Qur'an says the animal's flesh and blood don't reach God
22:37: the devotion from you is what reaches Him.

games.q: your family's share of Eid meat arrives. your uncle wants to freeze all of it for the month. what fits the Prophet's words?
o: freeze it all; it was paid for, so it belongs to the family.
eat some, give some to others, and store some.
give every bit away; keeping any of it spoils the sacrifice.
games.why: the Prophet said of the sacrifice: eat, feed others, and store some. the table is shared, and the family eats too.

practice: Look around for one thing you have more of than you need: food in the cupboard, a coat, an hour on Saturday. Decide who could have a share of it.
Keep your eyes on that thing, or on that person in your mind, for the rest of the sit.

carryVoice: Your line: what would I give? Abraham was asked, and a ram came instead. The year's rhythm, complete.
